correctness.rationale: The exact monomial ring has nine minimal-prime quotients \(\mathbb C[x,y]\), each normal. Its image in their product is exactly the families with matching restrictions along common coordinate axes. The conductor criterion applied to normalized-component idempotents forces every component polynomial to be divisible by its two plane coordinates, giving \(\mathfrak c=(ad,ae,af,bd,be,bf,cd,ce,cf)\); the converse follows from zero boundary restrictions. The conductor quotient is the reduced six-axis scheme, the normalization fibers have cardinalities \(1,3,9\), and exact Hilbert-series subtraction gives \(H_{\widetilde R/R}(t)=(8+4t)/(1-t)\), hence multiplicity \(12\). The packaged exact checker independently reproduces the finite combinatorial and Hilbert-function consequences.
